The sell-off, driven by a wipeout in tech and AI stocks, comes a day after Anthropic raised a staggering $81.34 billion during its IPO on Thursday, lifting the manufacturer's valuation to $1.414 trillion.

Anthropic shares were down 12% on Friday, giving back most of their gains after jumping 17% in their debut session.

Sevens Report Research's Tom Essaye said Thursday's sell-off primarily hit the tech sector, but added that "weakness is extending this morning and, like yesterday, pulling the broad market lower (although there was no latest negative news overnight in the tech sector).".

Concerns over inflation, a potential U.S. government shutdown in December, and continued conflict in the Middle East have kept some investors on edge. That, coupled with a recent spate of tech outages—including the FAA outage last Friday and the Microsoft outage last Thursday—have created a sense of unease among tech investors.

Recent findings suggest that AI investors were already feeling wary—as the burgeoning AI industry matures, it has yet to reach profitability. Anthropic reported $33.24 billion in revenue in the first three quarters of this year, but a $104 billion net loss for the same period.

One sector that is seemingly bucking the downward trend is real estate, which is performing better than the overall S&P 500. The S&P 500 Real Estate Sector is up 6.95% since the beginning of the year, while the overall S&P is up 3.15%.

Housing stocks—especially those of major homebuilders—have shown relative strength this month due to continued institutional investment from firms such as Berkshire Hathaway.

Despite headwinds for homebuilders, there are reasons for optimism following the midterm elections and the passage of the 21st Century Road to Housing Act, which passed with bipartisan support in July.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has warned of the rising risk of AI scams, including the use of deepfakes that impersonate Binance executives and staff.

The world's largest crypto exchange recently took to X to warn its users that improvements in artificial intelligence are making it harder to distinguish fake messages from real ones.

"AI deepfakes are making impersonation scams harder to spot," the crypto exchange mentioned in a post.

The cryptocurrency exchange has assured its customers that no one from Binance will ever reach out to them asking for money or offering unsolicited investment advice.

Binance indicates scammers are making realistic deepfake videos featuring executives and employees of the company.

Fraudsters are using these deepfakes, some of which are very realistic, to trick potential targets through fraudulent video calls.

That way, people who fall victim to the scam might think they are interacting with real Binance personnel.

Binance warned that scammers often try to reach potential targets through messaging apps such as WhatsApp or Telegram. They impersonate Binance employees by using their names, photos, and job titles to appear credible.

After making contact with a potential victim, the scammer may try to convince them to send crypto, take part in an exclusive investment opportunity, or take other financial actions.

Binance has called on crypto people to be cautious about any unexpected messages they receive, even if they seem to be from someone at the company they know.

A realistic appearance no longer guarantees a person's identity, given that AI can now easily mimic voices and facial expressions.

Users should double-check any suspicious messages through official Binance support channels before taking any action.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The head of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil has claimed that legitimately obtained money could be considered laundered if it’s used to purchase stablecoins.
  • The senior Brazilian official claimed that converting money into stablecoins could link it to money laundering, even when it was initially obtained legally.
  • According to a recent report, Gerson Romantini, who is the director of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil, allegedly made the controversial statements at a private event attended by representatives of financial companies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The head of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil has claimed that legitimately obtained money could be considered laundered if it’s used to purchase stablecoins.

The senior Brazilian official claimed that converting money into stablecoins could link it to money laundering, even when it was initially obtained legally.

According to a recent report, Gerson Romantini, who is the director of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil, allegedly made the controversial statements at a private event attended by representatives of financial companies.

Romantini claimed that funds acquired legally could be transformed once they enter the stablecoin ecosystem.

In his view, even legally obtained money could effectively be "dirtied" if used in certain stablecoin schemes, and thus be considered part of a money laundering operation.

It’s crucial to note that the comments attributed to Romantini do not represent an official statement that all conversions into stablecoins could be considered money laundering.

This statement comes as Brazil has already moved to tighten restrictions on how cryptocurrencies are used for international payments.

On April 30, the Central Bank of Brazil published Resolution No. 561, which took effect on Oct. 1.

The resolution limits the use of virtual assets for the settlement of international payment and transfer services, also known as eFX.

In practice, this means that payments between an eFX provider and its foreign partner must be settled through traditional foreign exchange operations or a Brazilian real account opened by nonresidents.

Crypto payments for these particular settlements are off-limits.

A practice called the "stablecoin sandwich" is particularly concerning.

The way it works is that a Brazilian fintech accepts a certain amount of reais from a customer, then uses this money to purchase stablecoins like USDT or USDC and sends the funds in crypto to an offshore company.

This firm, in turn, can convert these stablecoins into fiat currency to make payments or send money to families.

This allows users to make international money transfers for a lower fee and circumvent some of the infrastructure banks use.

The controversial statements have already received a response from Brazil’s crypto industry.

Sources indicate that in a statement on Nov. 14, the Brazilian Association of Tokenization and Digital Assets (ABToken) questioned the alleged classification of stablecoin transactions as money laundering.

ABToken maintains that the use of stablecoins is not necessarily illegal.

Furthermore, the association also cautioned that sweeping bans may create legal confusion and hinder legitimate business activities that use stablecoins for international payments.

Their HOA Approved Their Backyard Fences. Now They’re Being Told To Tear Them Down.

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that almost six years ago, Laura Burns-Sierra hired Home Depot to install a fence around her property in the Cypress Mill community near Tampa, FL.
  • Now, another organization claims the fence has to come down.
  • "We couldn't do anything, any construction, any fences, nothing, without HOA approval," Burns-Sierra tells Realtor.com®.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that almost six years ago, Laura Burns-Sierra hired Home Depot to install a fence around her property in the Cypress Mill community near Tampa, FL. She submitted the looks to her homeowners association, received written approval and had the fence professionally installed.

Now, another organization claims the fence has to come down.

"We couldn't do anything, any construction, any fences, nothing, without HOA approval," Burns-Sierra tells Realtor.com®. "I followed the procedures to the T.".

Recent findings suggest that burns-Sierra is among a group of homeowners in the Sun City Center neighborhood caught in an unusual dispute between their HOA and the Cypress Mill Community Development District, or CDD. The latter says fences installed within drainage easements are interfering with its ability to maintain the community's stormwater infrastructure and now need to be removed.

The conflict has left residents facing hundreds or even thousands of dollars in unexpected expenses—and raises an important question for homeowners everywhere:.

Is an HOA's written approval enough to protect you when another governing body has authority over your property?

At the center of the dispute is a distinction many homeowners may not realize exists.

An HOA generally oversees community standards, including architectural approvals, landscaping, and fence design. A CDD, meanwhile, is a special-purpose local government that can be responsible for infrastructure such as roads, drainage systems, and stormwater ponds.

In Cypress Mill, those responsibilities overlap on portions of homeowners' properties designated as drainage easements.

Jonathan Ellis, a Florida attorney experienced in HOA law—but is not involved in the dispute directly—tells Realtor.com that HOA approval doesn't necessarily authorize a homeowner to build within an easement.

Sources indicate that "The HOA is telling you we don't have an objection to the fence," Ellis explains. "That doesn't mean now you can build the fence and don't worry about federal law, municipal law, or requirements of the CDD.".

In other words, the HOA may have properly approved the fences under its own rules without resolving whether they complied with the district's separate requirements.

Ellis states the similar names of the HOA and CDD can add to the confusion, particularly for homeowners who aren't familiar with the distinction between the two organizations.

Burns-Sierra says the community's drainage ponds had been maintained for years without her fence becoming an concern.

She had her fence installed in May 2021, after receiving written approval from the HOA. About five years later, around Sept. 1, 2026, she and other residents received notice that the structure encroached on a drainage easement and would have to be removed by Sept. 18.

Burns-Sierra states maintenance contractors eventually arrived outside her home prepared to remove her fence and sought $625 for the work.

She refused, saying she wanted time to investigate the district's authority and understand why a fence that had been approved years earlier was suddenly unacceptable.

"I am not going to pay you no money to tear down my fence," she recalls telling the workers.

Neighbor Victor Abreu faced a similar predicament, although his circumstances were different.

Abreu tells Realtor.com that he received written HOA approval to install a gate connecting his home to an existing fence belonging to his neighbor.

When the CDD subsequently demanded that the structures obstructing the drainage easement be removed or relocated, Victor complied.

On Oct. 19 he paid a contractor $1,000 to install a fresh section of fencing closer to his house, losing part of a garden he estimates had cost approximately $1,500.

The new arrangement also created a wider opening between neighboring properties, raising concerns about privacy, security, and access to the pond behind their homes.

Victor says he believes communication broke down between the two organizations.

According to recent reports, "I would blame both of them," he indicates. "I would say 50-50.".

The Cypress Mill CDD maintains that the drainage easements are essential to the neighborhood's stormwater management system.

In a written response to Realtor.com, district counsel Whitney A. Sousa said the ponds and drainage areas are subject to environmental permits and oversight, including requirements administered by the Southwest Florida Water Management District.

The district has a legal responsibility to ensure contractors can inspect, maintain, and repair the system.

Mason Leon, the CDD’s on-site manager, tells Realtor.com that the fencing situation eventually made one pond inaccessible to the district's aquatic maintenance contractor through authorized access routes.

Industry observers note that according to Sousa, the issue was brought before the CDD board on Aug. 13, 2026. A subsequent review identified 11 properties with fences or other structures encroaching on drainage easements.

The district determined that the encroachments must be removed to preserve access for maintenance equipment, vehicles, and contractors.

Importantly, Sousa acknowledged that better coordination between the HOA and CDD might have prevented the dispute.

"Ideally, these easements would have been identified during the HOA's review process, and the CDD would have been contacted before the fences were approved or installed," she wrote.

The district aims to work with the HOA to clarify approval requirements going forward.

For homeowners already affected, however, the district expects them to cover the costs of removing or relocating their fences.

Sousa said residents requesting additional time have received extensions. The district does not believe those expenses should be spread across the neighborhood through CDD assessments.

Although residents are understandably frustrated, Ellis cautions against assuming the HOA is legally responsible simply because it approved their projects.

"Normally it's the unit owner that's responsible," he says, referring to securing all necessary permissions before construction.

Industry observers note that he explains that an HOA's approval generally addresses its own governing documents, including covenants, conditions, and restrictions. It doesn't eliminate the need to comply with separate drainage easements, building regulations, or other legal requirements.

Contractors may also have a role in identifying restrictions before beginning work.

Ellis notes that some communities permit fences within easements on the condition that homeowners remove them when access is needed.

The Cypress Mill CDD, however, has determined that all identified encroachments must be removed.

For homeowners like Burns-Sierra and Abreu, the distinction between an HOA's authority and the district's legal responsibilities has proved expensive.

The dispute offers a cautionary lesson for anyone purchasing a home or planning an outdoor renovation.

Ellis recommends determining which organizations have authority over a property before undertaking improvements.

"Homebuyers want to make sure when they're buying a home that they know of each of the entities that has a say over their property," he says.

Industry observers note that that means checking recorded plats, property surveys, and easement documents before installing fences, patios, pools, or other improvements. Homeowners should also determine whether approvals are required from an HOA, CDD, municipality, county, or utility provider.

And when multiple organizations are involved, written approval from one shouldn't be mistaken for permission from all of them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 17:17 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

It has been revealed that financial software company Intuit Inc. today announced that it has agreed to sell its Mailchimp email marketing business to Italian technology holding company Bending Spoons S.p.A. for about $3.68 billion.

It has been revealed that coming five years after Intuit agreed to acquire Mailchimp for $12 billion, the sale price is less than a third of what the company paid. The 2021 purchase was the largest in Intuit’s history at the time.

Recent findings suggest that although Bending Spoons describes the transaction as all-cash, Intuit will reinvest $368 million of its proceeds in newly issued Bending Spoons shares. That leaves Intuit with $3.31 billion in cash from the sale, according to the companies. Included in the deal is The Rocket Science Group LLC, the legal entity behind Mailchimp. Closing is expected in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

In a recent development, selling Mailchimp is remarked to sharpen Intuit’s focus on the artificial intelligence-native tools it has built to help businesses win newly introduced customers, manage their pipeline and grow. Once the deal closes, Intuit intends to use the cash proceeds to buy back its own shares before the end of fiscal 2027.

Jack Tam, a senior vice president at Intuit, noted the organization is confident Bending Spoons “will lead Mailchimp to continued success in this next chapter.”.

Growth at Mailchimp has stalled in recent quarters. Revenue from the business fell 1% to $313 million in the quarter ended Oct. 31. Intuit’s full-year guidance has Mailchimp revenue coming in flat to down 1%. In November 2024, Chief Financial Officer Sandeep Aujla told analysts that Intuit was seeing higher churn from smaller Mailchimp customers.

Sources indicate that “Mailchimp is a powerful brand, built over two decades of reshaping the email marketing category and redefining how companies grow their audiences,” noted Luca Ferrari, co-founder and chief executive of Bending Spoons. “We’re honored to welcome it to Bending Spoons and excited about what we can accomplish together.”.

Ferrari added that Bending Spoons plans to invest substantially in Mailchimp after closing. According to Bending Spoons, the transformation of a business it acquires is typically deep, entailing reorganized teams, overhauled technology and redesigned user interfaces.

Founded in 2013, Bending Spoons has built a portfolio of digital businesses that includes AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Tractive, Vimeo and WeTransfer. Since listing on the Nasdaq in July, the tech giant has also completed acquisitions of Airtable Inc. for $1.285 billion and whiteboard platform Miro for $1.355 billion.

According to recent reports, intuit unveiled the sale alongside its fiscal 2027 first-quarter results. For the quarter, it reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.91, up 56% from $1.87 in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $4.35 billion, up 12% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting adjusted earnings of $2.70 per share on revenue of $4.31 billion.

In a recent development, for its fiscal second quarter, Intuit expects adjusted earnings per share of $3.17 to $3.22 on revenue of $4.93 billion to $4.95 billion. Intuit lowered its full-year revenue guidance to between $23.08 billion and $23.37 billion.

In a recent development, behind the cut is Credit Karma, the company’s personal finance and credit score service, which is now forecast to grow 3% to 7% this fiscal year, down from 11% to 13% previously. Intuit reiterated its full-year adjusted earnings guidance of $22.88 to $23.12 per share. None of the guidance includes the effect of the Mailchimp sale.

Intuit shares fell more than 10% in after-hours trading.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has published a lengthy post on EIP-8037, a change planned for the Glamsterdam upgrade. In his latest post, Buterin wrote that something like EIP-8037 is, unfortunately, the only way for Ethereum to scale safely.

Industry observers note that with the update, Ethereum will collect an additional gas fee for the creation of new accounts. Creating a new account would cost more than five times as much gas as it does now, with new storage slots and contracts getting more expensive too.

According to Buterin, execution is easy to scale, but Ethereum's state already grows by around 110 GiB per year, and every node has to keep it.

Unfortunately, it will bring more pressure on existing contracts, for example, the OP Stack bridge. The bridge has a hardcoded gas limit of 40,000, and even a small increase in state gas costs would push its operation above it. Mainnet has at least 13 contracts like that, according to the security firm ChainSecurity.

It's a double-edged sword: from one standpoint, it limits the ability of spammers and scammers to fill the network with junk accounts used by illicit actors; from the other, it creates additional financial pressure.

Glamsterdam being postponed is another pain factor here: considering the poor state of the market and Ethereum's struggle, it's clear that any delays in major updates negatively affect the network outlook. The new date is yet to be confirmed.

Vitalik Buterin has been hinting at the change in gas consumption for ages now. Back in 2024, he called multidimensional gas the hardest problem in his own post on the topic.

Setting strict limits was never a farsighted option, and developers have been told that for years. However, it's yet another question: who's actually to blame? Buterin himself admitted that this rule hasn't been written down or repeated since 2021, so newer developers simply didn't know about it.

He now suggests writing down a list of features that are likely to change, from gas mechanics to slot time.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin price is getting hammered in the aftermath of the FOMC minutes. Gold isn’t doing much better; oil and stocks have joined the sell-off. The markets are already nervous about the Federal Reserve’s next decision, and yesterday’s FOMC minutes gave us another reason to worry: policymakers are still talking about raising interest rates.

Almost all officials saw further hikes as appropriate under their baseline outlook. Two even floated the possibility of a bigger increase if inflation refuses to cool.

This is a nasty combination for markets. Bitcoin fell around 3.2% over 24 hours, gold futures dropped more than 3%, and WTI crude lost around 3%. The dollar climbed to a 19-month high. Wall Street was mixed, though, with the Nasdaq finishing higher while the Dow and S&P 500 slipped.

Here’s the comparison. In March 2020, the Fed was slashing rates, buying bonds and throwing emergency liquidity at a financial system under immense pressure. Congress approved a $2.2 trillion rescue package to keep households and businesses afloat.

Today, we are watching markets fall while the Fed is possibly making money more expensive.

Sources indicate that october’s FOMC minutes weren’t exactly what markets wanted to hear. The Fed held rates at 3.75%–4% during its October meeting, but almost all participants believed further increases would likely be appropriate. Two officials also said a hike larger than the usual 25 basis points could be considered if inflation data came in hotter than expected.

Industry observers note that and there was more in those minutes than just interest rates. Officials raised concerns about hedge fund leverage and the growing debt tied to artificial intelligence investments. Some financing arrangements could become a problem if investors start questioning enormous AI spending, and whether it will generate the returns companies expect.

Sources indicate that the risk is forced selling. Leveraged funds facing losses or investor withdrawals may have to dump assets swiftly, potentially pushing prices down further.

Gold has its own problem. A stronger dollar and higher interest rates make it less attractive to investors who can earn a return elsewhere. Bitcoin price, meanwhile, remains vulnerable when traders cut exposure to speculative assets.

According to recent reports, the Fed hasn’t declared a financial emergency. Its minutes actually describe the banking system as resilient. But officials are clearly paying attention to risks that could amplify a market shock.

Discover: The Best Token Presales.

March 2020 was brutal. COVID-19 lockdowns brought businesses to a standstill. Investors rushed for cash, stocks collapsed, and Bitcoin briefly slipped below $4,000 after sitting near $10,000 just weeks earlier.

Sources indicate that the Federal Reserve didn’t wait around. It cut rates by 50 basis points on March 3, then delivered another 100-basis-point cut on March 15. The federal funds target range dropped to 0%–0.25%.

According to recent reports, on March 23, the Fed announced unlimited purchases of Treasury securities and mortgage-backed securities, promising to buy whatever amounts were necessary to support market functioning. It also introduced emergency lending programmes to keep credit flowing.

Industry observers note that president Donald Trump signed the $2.2 trillion CARES Act on March 27. The package included direct payments to eligible Americans, expanded unemployment benefits, and assistance for businesses struggling to survive lockdowns. The Paycheck Protection Program gave small businesses access to loans designed to help them keep employees on payroll.

In a recent development, the response was enormous, but the economy was facing an extraordinary shutdown. Millions of Americans had lost their jobs, businesses were closing, and normal economic activity had practically disappeared.

Markets eventually bounced back. The S&P 500 recovered its pre-pandemic record by August 2020. Bitcoin climbed above $12,000 during the same month.

Recent findings suggest that the current US economy isn’t in the same position as it was during the pandemic. Inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target, and policymakers are discussing rate increases rather than cuts.

In a recent development, slashing rates to zero and flooding markets with liquidity might help asset prices. It could also make inflation worse. Another multitrillion-dollar spending package would face an entirely different argument in Congress, especially without a pandemic-style economic shutdown.

The Fed doesn’t have to choose between doing nothing and repeating the 2020 rescue. If banks struggle to fund themselves or credit markets start freezing, it can step in with emergency lending and liquidity operations. That’s a much narrower response than another round of unlimited bond purchases.

The Fed’s concerns about leveraged hedge funds and AI financing could become more relevant if investors start selling indiscriminately. A market correction is one thing. Forced selling spreading through the financial system is another.

At the moment, there’s no evidence that we’re facing another March 2020. The banking system remains resilient, and falling Bitcoin prices alone won’t trigger a government bailout.

But the Fed has a problem that didn’t exist in quite the same way during the pandemic. It may need to protect financial stability without giving up its fight against inflation. In 2020, Washington opened the taps. This time, we wait and see, and Bitcoin price will survive.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Major U.S. wealth management company EP Wealth Advisors has revealed that it holds an investment in an XRP exchange-traded fund (ETF). This was disclosed in the company's latest 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

EP Wealth Advisors, a California-based investment advisory firm with about $24.4 billion in securities holdings, has revealed that it held 18,400 shares in the Volatility Shares XRP ETF (XRPI) as of Sept. 30, 2026.

This was disclosed in the official SEC filing that the company submitted to the commission on Nov. 13. The filing revealed that the investment was valued at $147,936 at the end of the third quarter.

According to recent reports, furthermore, the filing showed that the total portfolio value reported by EP Wealth Advisors stood at $24,380,879,896. This value comprises 1,603 items in the organization's 13F information table.

It's worth noting, however, that this isn't the company's total assets under management. It's the value of its reportable securities holdings. There are also assets that are not included in Form 13F.

Interestingly, this isn't the first time EP Wealth Advisors has held an investment in XRPI. Data from its historical 13F filings highlights that in the second quarter of 2026, the wealth management organization held 13,425 shares in XRPI.

In a recent development, the recent filing indicates that the company has now increased the number of shares it holds in the XRP ETF by 4,975 shares. This represents about a 37% increase in the company's XRPI holdings during the third quarter.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, this amount is very small relative to the firm's multibillion-dollar securities portfolio. It represents less than 0.01% of the total value of its reported securities holdings.

It's also worth reiterating that Form 13F is simply a filing that indicates institutional holdings at the end of a quarter. It doesn't necessarily represent the investment manager's current holdings.

The Volatility Shares XRP ETF was introduced in May 2025. Its ticker symbol is XRPI, and it is currently trading on Nasdaq.

Sources indicate that XRPI isn't a spot XRP ETF. This means it doesn't directly hold the cryptocurrency XRP. Rather, it primarily derives its exposure to XRP's price movements through XRP futures contracts.

Industry observers note that this ETF essentially provides investors with a way to invest in XRP without actually having to hold or custody the cryptocurrency. The ETF aims to deliver investment returns that correlate with the performance of XRP.

According to recent reports, as of Nov. 13, the most recent available data from the fund issuer shows that XRPI's net assets stood at about $77.9 million.

Schwartz wrote that he "really doesn't like risk." According to Schwartz, he and his wife agreed years ago to sell some of their coins every time crypto reached a fresh all-time high. In 2025, Schwartz sold around 2.5 million XRP and paid about $1.7 million in capital gains tax on the sale. He had received these tokens in 2020 and 2023.

Schwartz also stated that he was a skeptic from the start and did not believe in the early price records of crypto. "When XRP hit 10 cents, that seemed ridiculous. When ETH hit $1, that seemed ridiculous," he wrote.

In his view, the price of XRP today depends on overall sentiment in the crypto market, and fees on the network barely move it. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • The malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on Tuesday through Microsoft’s own publisher account, giving them the appearance of a routine revision to a package that sees close to 200,000 downloads a month.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 17:44 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Microsoft Corp.’s official Python package for its Agent Framework artificial intelligence agent toolkit was compromised earlier this week, as an attacker published two malicious versions to the Python Package Index that were designed to steal cloud and developer credentials.

The malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on Tuesday through Microsoft’s own publisher account, giving them the appearance of a routine revision to a package that sees close to 200,000 downloads a month. Both versions were pulled from PyPI within about an hour, but anyone who installed them in that window is at risk.

Researchers at cloud security firm Wiz Inc. have since found that the attacker appears to have gained publishing access using a client certificate and private key for Microsoft’s Engineering System Release Pipeline, an internal service the company uses to sign and publish packages. Address filtering on the service blocked the attacker’s first attempt from Amazon Web Services, according to Wiz, though the attacker was able to publish on a second try from Microsoft-owned address space.

How the attacker obtained the credentials is not known. Microsoft had not responded to a request for comment from BleepingComputer as of Wednesday.

The researchers also observed part of the operation, as the attacker’s tooling was reporting its progress to the same public webhook it was using to collect stolen data. The tooling identified itself as Cairn, an open-source penetration-testing framework that uses AI.

The malware itself is delivered through a .pth file added to both releases, a type of file Python runs every time it starts, meaning the credential stealer runs even if the framework itself is never imported. The two versions also kept the genuine agent-framework-core 1.26.0 as a dependency, so the framework continued to work normally while the malware ran in the background.

In a recent development, once running, the malware collects secrets from environment variables and from other running processes, along with credential files for services such as Azure, npm, Git, Docker and Hugging Face. It also requests Azure managed identity tokens for 12 resources, according to application security firm Endor Labs Inc., with the second version adding requests for GitHub Actions tokens. The stolen data is then compressed, encoded and sent to a webhook.site address controlled by the attacker.

Researchers at malware tracking site OpenSourceMalware described the malware as a “focused credential and token stealer, not a remote access trojan,” noting that it does not install any persistence on infected systems.

It has been revealed that wiz’s analysis suggests the number of victims may be small, though it covers only the 50 requests the attacker’s free webhook.site account retained. Of those, 17 represented only three unique successful thefts of victim data, with the rest coming from the attacker’s own machines and from sandbox and security vendor scanning.

The incident is not the first this year involving an official Microsoft Python package. In May, Microsoft’s durabletask package was hijacked after its PyPI token was stolen in an attack that has been linked to TeamPCP, the group also behind the compromise of LiteLLM. Wiz claims it has not linked the two incidents.

Anyone who installed either of the malicious versions is being urged to treat it as a credential compromise, according to researchers, who recommend rebuilding from version 1.26.0 and rotating any secrets the affected systems could access.

“A list of dependencies in production might show no trace of the framework, while a build runner could have installed it and been shut down before the alert arrived,” James Matchett, head of security at software supply chain security company Cloudsmith Ltd., told SiliconANGLE.

“If that runner had access to a deployment token, the team needs to know which version it installed and what the token could access,” he added.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • That’s the question at the center of a growing debate in Clark County, NV, where water is scarce and locals are skeptical about a luxury development's proposal to create a massive water feature.
  • It has been revealed that joel Laub and his partner, Randall Jones, began developing the Reserve at Red Rock Canyon in 2022, aiming to create a high-end luxury community amid the Nevada wilderness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that should a private developer have the ability to build a human-made pond in the middle of a drought-stricken region? What if that developer says that firefighters can access the pond to fight wildfires?

That’s the question at the center of a growing debate in Clark County, NV, where water is scarce and locals are skeptical about a luxury development's proposal to create a massive water feature.

It has been revealed that joel Laub and his partner, Randall Jones, began developing the Reserve at Red Rock Canyon in 2022, aiming to create a high-end luxury community amid the Nevada wilderness. The Reserve is being built on 65 acres that were once home to the Bonnie Springs Ranch, a historic, Old West-themed family resort that once featured horseback riding and a small zoo.

Sources indicate that two-acre empty plots in the community start at $7.5 million. But that’s not what has the community up in arms. Instead, it’s what the Reserve is touting on its website: a large human-made pond in the middle of the property.

It has been revealed that to outsiders, it seems like just one feature in a long list of amenities. But for some locals in Clark County, which was declared a natural disaster area due to drought earlier this year, the pond seems like a slap in the face—even as the developers attempt to position it as a fire safety "dip pond.".

“This little dip pond here is really fire safety as an afterthought, and I think that’s pretty obvious in terms of even their planning,” said Sarah J. McCrea-Dameron, a Blue Diamond, NV, resident and former deputy fire chief from Las Vegas Fire & Rescue, at a zoning commission meeting this past week. “It’s not in an area that’s necessary, and it’s not the best use of that water and that precious resource for our community.“.

The Reserve at Red Rock Canyon development sits within the Red Rock Canyon Conservation Area, an expansive 195,000-acre area within the Mojave Desert. Aztec sandstone foundations dating back to 180 million years can be found in the area, along with sea fossils and hundreds of local bird species. More than 3 million people visit the area each year.

Recent findings suggest that water for the area is supplied by the Colorado River. In recent years, the river and the several lakes it feeds have been pushed to the limit, as upcoming development, coupled with more frequent droughts, have strained resources.

The river doesn’t just supply necessary water to communities across the Southwest: It also produces much-needed hydropower for the region.

Earlier this year, Lake Powell, one of the lakes fed by the Colorado River, dropped to its lowest level in history, threatening to shut down the Glen Canyon Dam, which supplies power to Wyoming, Utah, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona, Nevada, and Nebraska.

It has been revealed that communities around the Red Rock Canyon Conservation Area take the mantle of water conservation seriously. In fact, in 2020, the nearby community of Blue Diamond issued a temporary moratorium on “the issuance of additional water commitments” that remains in place.

Now, as the developers Laub and Jones offer unbuilt lots in their upcoming development for $7.5 million, they are pitching the proposed pond as a neighborhood amenity.

“Paths and roads will meander past water features fed by the canyon’s natural springs,” the development’s website states.

According to recent reports, but those types of features are typically prohibited by Clark County’s Title 30, which governs building and development in the area. Title 30 at the moment prohibits the creation of human-made lakes of any size and water features greater than 10 square feet of surface area. So the developers stressed that the human-made pond would be fed via private water rights, and therefore not impede on community resources. Instead of using Colorado River resources, the project would be fed using groundwater.

Bob Gronauer, the developers' lawyer, said the water feature would be a “dip pond”—a water source for use by firefighting helicopters. Wildfires are a frequent problem in the region. In 2025 alone, there were 619 fires in the state, which destroyed more than 368,000 acres.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, the developers have already signed a use agreement with the Nevada Division of Forestry. The developers claimed the NDF came to them to ask them to create the pond, but the NDF said the developers approached them about the partnership, the Nevada Independent reported.

"We reached out to the Bureau of Land Management Red Rock management staff at the visitor center, Save Red Rock, Friends of Red Rock, as well as the Nature Conservancy Nevada immediately upon purchasing the property to work with them to make this development compatible with the Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area," Laub tells Realtor.com. (Laub is the chairman of the Nature Conservancy board.).

Laub indicates the idea for the dip pond actually came from the BLM.

According to recent reports, "They asked if we could work with them on fire management in Red Rock Canyon, and would we consider providing water for firefighting. Of course our answer was yes. We have a 220,000-gallon water tank designed into our water system for supplying water to our fire hydrants, and we agreed to provide a fire hydrant for the BLM water tankers to fill up in the event of a wildfire," Laub continues.

"The ponds are designed to fit into the canyon ecosystem and look natural but also to be compatible with helicopter firefighting.".

Laub tells Realtor.com that they've already been testing the wells in the canyon, and "none of the testing results from these wells has indicated a draw down of significance from our use of the water system.".

He also notes that they purchased the water rights from Bonnie Springs Ranch, which had been in use for more than 60 years.

"The property has had ponds, streams, pools, and springs from the original ranch in 1952," he explains.

To expedite the creation of the dip pools, the developers proposed an amendment to Title 30 that would add language permitting “a body of water, served from standalone private water rights, within 1,000 feet of a National Conservation Area, intended for fire suppression and life safety purposes as agreed upon with a State or Federal Agency.”In October, Clark County Planning Commission's professional staff recommended denying the amendment.

"As proposed, there is no indication of how these water features would be designed, the capacity of these water features, or other potential uses for the stored water. The proliferation of non-essential water features will place an additional burden on the existing water supply," the staff recommendation read. "Furthermore, this request may encourage additional non-essential water features within residential and nonresidential development.".

However, the Planning Commission approved the amendment by a vote of 6-1. It then went to the Clark County Zoning Board for approval. On Wednesday night, during the public comment period of the meeting, around a dozen community members spoke out against the planned feature.

“You can design a decorative water feature and then call it a dip pond. You can offer to let the Forest Service use it knowing that they never will because of the way it’s designed and location, but that doesn’t make that decorative water feature a piece of critical fire infrastructure," remarked former Clark County Fire Capt. Erik Klausen.

“They’re trying to put a plastic fire helmet on this water feature and tell us it’s about public safety,” he continued.

At the end of the public comment period, all seven commissioners voted in favor of the proposed amendment, though, as Commissioner Justin Jones noted, the approval of the amendment does not mean the dip pond project has been approved.

Furthermore, noted Commissioner Marilyn Kirkpatrick, the project needs to be fit for purpose.

Industry observers note that "If it's a fire-suppression pond, then it has to be a fire-suppression pond in my mind," stated Kirkpatrick. "It should stay as a fire-supression pond, not as a recreational venue, not as irrigation, because that water is supposed to be there for a reason.".

Realtor.com has reached out to developer Jones and lawyer Gronauer for comment.

XRP Ledger Foundation Director of Community Hussein Zangana (Vet) shared a tidbit of XRPL's early history in a recent X post.

Vet noted that the XRP Ledger (XRPL) still carries traces of Satoshi Nakamoto’s original Bitcoin design, highlighting two features.

In 2011, three engineers—David Schwartz, Jed McCaleb, and Arthur Britto—began developing the XRP Ledger (XRPL). Fascinated by Bitcoin, they set out to create a better version that improved upon its limitations—with the goal of creating a digital asset that was more sustainable and built specifically for payments.

As reported, the first line of code for the core of what would become the XRP Ledger (XRPL) was written by David Schwartz, who is Ripple CTO emeritus, about 15 years ago, on November 11, 2011.

It has been revealed that vet delves into the earliest part of XRP Ledger history, noting that 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, wrote. Vet added that Jed McCaleb also copied Satoshi’s timekeeping code into the XRPL, even including one of the Bitcoin creator’s comments shared as a screenshot.

Did you know all of us on the XRP Ledger use design choices by Satoshi daily? 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Satoshi wrote. Jed copied Satoshi's timekeeping code into the XRPL, including one of Satoshi's comments. By the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone. In December 2014, Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment. Two design choices of Satoshi still remain on the XRPL and all of us use at least one of it. Signature curve secp256k1 (we also support Ed25519 thus not everyone uses this) and how XRPL addresses are generated from the public key with SHA-256 followed by RIPEMD-160, that's what all of us use.

The quote "Never go to sea with two chronometers; take one or three" is a classic maritime adage famously included by Satoshi Nakamoto (the pseudonymous creator of Bitcoin) within the Bitcoin source code.

Vet explained that by the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone from the XRP Ledger. In December 2014, former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment.

However, two of Satoshi's design choices still remain on the XRP Ledger: the first is the secp256k1 signature curve, which Bitcoin uses and which the XRP Ledger continues to support. However, the ledger also supports Ed25519, meaning not every XRPL user relies on secp256k1.

"I remember David saying they used secp256k1 so no one would doubt the security because it's the same as Bitcoin's, etc.," Vet stated, citing the insight of the Ripple CTO emeritus on secp256k1, adding, "Lots of interesting things to dig into from the early days.".

According to recent reports, the second is the method used to generate XRP Ledger addresses from public keys. The process applies SHA-256 hashing followed by RIPEMD-160, a design inherited from Bitcoin that remains common to all XRPL addresses.

Asked why the timekeeping code and Satoshi's comment were removed, Vet explained that this became leftover code as new code was introduced, so it was cleaned up.

Cardano DReps have rejected a proposal by Toto Finance to spend 22 million ADA from the Cardano treasury on a "Strategic Copper Reserve.".

The vote closed on Nov. 15, and DReps holding 2.86 billion ADA voted against the proposal, according to Cardano governance data. DReps with 20.02 million ADA voted in favor of it.

DRep John MacPherson was among those who voted "No," and he explained his decision in a post on X.

Industry observers note that macPherson wrote that he is not against real-world assets on Cardano. Still, he said the proposal asks the treasury "to take on both the copper price and the ada price," and Toto Finance would collect "up to about 3.4M ada in fees.".

At the same time, MacPherson remarked that the proposal is “more honest about its risks than most.”.

Toto Finance, a organization led by Monty Metzger, submitted the proposal on Oct. 15. ADA is trading at $0.152 on Monday, and the requested 22 million ADA is now worth around $3.3 million.

The plan was to buy copper with 14.72 million ADA and store it in a warehouse near New Orleans. Toto Finance wanted to issue one CuTT token for each pound of copper. The metal would be sold in 18 to 24 months.

The Cardano Foundation, which votes as a DRep, announced its "No" vote in October.

"We recognize the opportunity in real-world asset tokenization; however, this proposal places 22,000,000 ada under the recipient's sole control to fund a fee-heavy concentrated commodity position whose safeguards are not yet in place," the foundation wrote.

Three members of the Constitutional Committee voted "No," and the other four members did not vote.

Sources indicate that crypto commentator Ingeniero Cripto agreed with MacPherson in the replies under his post. He called the "double exposure" to the prices of copper and ADA the key problem of the proposal, as the Cardano treasury already holds ADA.

According to him, RWAs on Cardano make sense, but “funding the asset itself is a different question than funding the rails.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:11 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

In a recent development, incident remediation company Resolve AI Inc. has declared the launch of SRE-1, a new model that has been trained to find the root cause of production alerts, and Primary On-call, a new service that puts its artificial intelligence agents on call ahead of human engineers.

It has been revealed that the new model, announced Wednesday, reflects the tech giant’s argument that while AI has transformed how software gets written, it has barely touched how software gets run. According to Resolve AI, production has no public training corpus to match the published code that models learned from, as incidents at each company stay private.

SRE-1 is a 27 billion-parameter model built on open weights and trained by a team of 16 AI researchers over a final run of 7.4 days on up to 512 graphics processing units. Measured on the same incidents before and after training, which used reinforcement learning alone, the pass rate for a single investigation rose from 6.9% to 38.8%.

Resolve AI used Snowflake Inc.’s Cortex Training, a serverless service for customizing open-weight models, to build SRE-1. Snowflake Senior Vice President of Engineering Vivek Raghunathan said Resolve AI was the first design partner for the service.

In testing on 49 difficult live production cases, each run five times, an ensemble of five SRE-1 investigations matched the strongest frontier model tested at a lower cost, according to the manufacturer. Resolve AI also benchmarked its complete system on 178 production alert investigations, solving about twice as many incidents as general-purpose coding agents.

Primary On-call puts that research to work on the critical path. Each page is investigated across telemetry, infrastructure, code and operational knowledge, according to the firm. Depending on what it finds, the agent can close the alert, mitigate the problem where a team’s policies permit or escalate to a human. Once it has acted, the agent checks the fix against the production baseline, monitoring it until recovery holds.

The agent also links related alerts and investigations into a shared view of each underlying problem. For teams wary of handing over the pager straight away, Resolve AI offers a shadow mode that records the call the agent would have made on each page.

According to recent reports, up to 80% of paged alerts in production are said to be handled by Primary On-call without escalation. Customers have reported a tenfold improvement in mean time to resolution, along with root-cause accuracy of up to 95%, according to Resolve AI.

Sources indicate that salesforce Inc. is among the early customers. Bhupesh Patel, a software engineering principal architect at Salesforce, said that in the first few weeks of dark launch testing, the agent closed more than 70% of the CRM Analytics team’s paging alerts “without waking an engineer.”.

Recent findings suggest that “No engineering team can keep up with how fast code and patches land in production,” said Resolve AI Chief Executive Spiros Xanthos. “The answer is agents that are accurate and fast enough to sit on the critical path, and that takes a model built for production.”.

Primary On-call is now generally available. Access to SRE-1 is limited to Resolve AI’s own platform.

In a recent development, resolve AI is a venture capital-backed startup that has raised more than $190 million to date, including a $40 million extension to its Series A round in April, led by DST Global and Salesforce Ventures, that valued the tech giant at $1.5 billion. Notable customers include Coinbase Global Inc., DoorDash Inc., Figma Inc., MSCI Inc., Nasdaq Inc., SAP SE and Zscaler Inc.

Industry observers note that solana has officially removed the "beta" tag from its mainnet's name and introduced the Solana 1.0 standard. The switch was announced on Nov. 16 at the Breakpoint conference in London.

"Solana 1.0 marks the network's graduation from 'mainnet beta' to 'mainnet,' retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch," the Solana Foundation noted.

Solana launched on March 16, 2020, and the network had been working under the "mainnet-beta" label for six years and eight months. According to the foundation, the label "never evolved to signal its production status.".

It has been revealed that the Solana Foundation coordinated the rollout with the Anza and Firedancer teams. Co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko replied to the announcement on X with three exploding-head emojis.

It has been revealed that "For people, this is the same network, nothing changes. Your SOL, accounts, assets, applications, and transaction history remain the same," the foundation wrote. On Monday, SOL is trading at $71.35.

It has been revealed that according to the foundation, two upgrades made the change possible. In October, Solana activated Alpenglow with the Agave 4.3 release, and the time to final confirmation went down by almost 99%, from 12.8 seconds to around 150 milliseconds.

According to recent reports, firedancer, a validator client developed by Jump Crypto independently from Agave, is also now running on the Solana mainnet. Independent implementations "limit the impact of bugs affecting one client, and strengthen network resilience," the foundation said.

Solana 1.0 also gives the network a shared protocol version, and it does not depend on the version numbers of individual clients such as Agave and Firedancer.

Industry observers note that "A shared protocol version lets everyone refer to Solana's evolution without using one client's release number as shorthand for the entire network," the Solana Foundation explained. "Announcing a protocol version does not activate every associated improvement at once.".

Recent findings suggest that earlier this year, Solana raised the compute limit per block from 60 million to 100 million compute units in May, and the slot time went down from 400 to 200 milliseconds in August. The maximum transaction size also went up from 1,232 to 4,096 bytes.

"Documentation, websites, explorers, and other ecosystem surfaces will progressively reflect the updated designation," the foundation added.

Jumping out of a helicopter into water below, rappelling down a 22-story building, enduring chemical warfare gas exposure — if you’ve never seen Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test, these are just a few of the tasks that must be completed.

It’s a reality TV show in which celebrities do physical challenges from the actual Special Forces selection process playbook. It’s like a competition show, but there are no eliminations, and no one gets voted off.

Industry observers note that to leave, participants must voluntarily withdraw, be medically withdrawn by a DS (directing staff) due to injury or be dismissed for refusing a direct order. During the final test, the DS ejects those who fail the interrogation or selection test.

Recent findings suggest that season 5 is set in the Malaysian jungle. It features Candace Cameron Bure, Brandi Glanville, Oliver Hudson, Ruby Rose, George Santos, Bre Tiesi, Matt Barnes, and Mauricio and Alexia Umansky, among others.

According to recent reports, at the time that this article was published, Alexia was still in the competition. Mauricio voluntarily withdrew after a rib injury sustained during a hand-to-hand fighting challenge with former NBA player Matt Barnes. Mauricio said the injury took two or three months to heal.

The following challenge involved gas, and Mauricio didn’t think his ribs could take it. He said he feared having a bad lung injury in the Malaysian jungle. Alexia agreed with the decision, saying the gas was the “most painful thing” she’d ever experienced in her life.

Inman spoke to Mauricio and Alexia midway through the season about the experience, the latest industry news and what’s next for The Agency.

What follows is the conversation, edited for length and clarity.

According to recent reports, I think for me, 100 percent, the heat. I think I anticipated intense heat and intense humidity, but you don’t know what it’s like until you really feel it … It was so unbearably hot, and in our barracks that we slept in, there was no windows, and when you were inside, you actually couldn’t tell like what was even happening out there. But it was almost like … “Good, let me be locked in this metal box because the outside is crazy.”.

Mauricio: I think for me, it was just the intensity of what a jungle really is. The first day we got there … when we were all showering and waiting to shower, there was a scorpion crawling on my leg, about to go in my boot, which I felt it and took it off just in the nick of time. Because if it went in my boot, it would have stung me, no question, right?

Recent findings suggest that alexia: It’s so hard to choose because literally every single thing was hard. Part of me wanted to say the car rides leading up to each challenge, because we didn’t know what was coming, and it was always so intense in the car. My heart would start pounding … the bottom line is the hardest part is just making sure that your mindset is correct [in] doing all these things and waking up each day and moving forward because that’s really what gets going is just moving forward and choosing to keep on going.

It has been revealed that mauricio: Yeah, I think Alexia nailed it. I mean, for me, it was really all about the little victories. The only way to survive is by looking at small victories, small steps … we used to say just make it to the next meal, just make it to the next day, just make it to tonight.

For me, the hardest part was leaving, was having to voluntarily withdraw. I did not want to have a medical withdrawal, so I didn’t want to go see the doctor and have them withdraw me.

Mauricio: Not one thing for me. What about you, Alexia?

Alexia: No. There’s nothing about this that’s easy.

Alexia: We loved everybody so much. I mean, we still talk all the time, and we still love each other so much. The words of affirmation we all told each other to this day are so special … But I think my first answer would have to be Candace [Cameron] Bure … she’s so strong, and we got looped together for a bunch of things because of our height similarities.

Mauricio: Well, I have to say that the person who surprised me the most was Alexia … the strength of her mind, her strength and what she did was extraordinary.

Traveling Home for Thanksgiving? How Smart Buyers Turn Holiday Visits Into Neighborhood Recon

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • That’s why it’s no surprise that the latest Migration Trends report by the National Association of Realtors® found that 30% of buyers who relocated did so to be near family.
  • Whether the goal is to care for aging parents, assist with childcare, or simply enjoy more time with loved ones, living near family can make a positive difference in everyday life.
  • If you’ve been contemplating buying a home closer to family, your Thanksgiving visit could be the perfect opportunity to start exploring what life in a fresh area could look like.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For most people, family is everything.

That’s why it’s no surprise that the latest Migration Trends report by the National Association of Realtors® found that 30% of buyers who relocated did so to be near family.

Whether the goal is to care for aging parents, assist with childcare, or simply enjoy more time with loved ones, living near family can make a positive difference in everyday life.

If you’ve been contemplating buying a home closer to family, your Thanksgiving visit could be the perfect opportunity to start exploring what life in a fresh area could look like.

Since you’re already making the trip, it only makes sense to get a firsthand look at the neighborhoods, homes, and local amenities to help you determine whether the move is worthwhile for your budget and lifestyle.

“Seeing how a community operates when people are home, traffic is heavier, and daily routines are stressed can help you make an informed decision about where to plant roots,” says Cameron Walker, real estate expert and manager of the agent network at Clever Real Estate in St. Louis.

Once you arrive in town for Thanksgiving, take a commute during rush hour.

Then, walk around the area during the day and at night and check out local shops, restaurants, parks, and other attractions.

“Be sure to speak to locals about traffic, parking, safety, noise, and other concerns that might arise during different seasons,” states Walker.

Pay attention to all the small details that will matter if you make the move: sidewalk length and quality, road conditions, street parking availability, cell service reliability, distance to the nearest airport, and proximity to hospitals.

If you have time, you may also want to attend a few open houses and meet with a real estate agent.

According to recent reports, “Look at homes for sale, recent home sales, and the length of time homes are taking to sell, as well as how many price reductions are being made. Learn about local property taxes, insurance costs, and whether there are many homes for sale that fit your price range,” Walker adds.

In addition, focus on schools, childcare, commute times, and other amenities to make sure you’d feel comfortable with your daily routines.

Recent findings suggest that in the late fall and early winter, typical buyer activity drops off sharply in many markets. That’s why it’s a great time to look for a home.

Depending on the market, it may open the doors to some unique negotiation leverage.

“As fewer and fewer buyers are ‘in the market’ from Thanksgiving to the New Year, sellers may become more flexible in their terms,” says Sander Scott, owner and broker of Net Real Estate in Traverse City, MI.

And there may be even more opportunities this year.

According to the Realtor.com® October 2026 housing report, approximately 1 in 5 listings had a price reduction, while active inventory was up 7.4% compared to last year.

That means you might have more housing options at your disposal and sellers may be more willing to adjust their asking prices.

“Focus on the right location and daily function. After all, saving money on a house that makes the childcare or caregiving goal harder to achieve defeats the purpose,” Scott adds.

In addition, think of a refinance as a potential bonus—not your proposal.

Industry observers note that “Rates come and go, but the purchase price is forever. Always consider the purchase price, the monthly payment, and whether you can afford it in the long run,” explains Walker.

Look beyond the monthly mortgage payment and understand the total cost of ownership. Being close to family is no fun if it forces you to become house poor as a result.

“Thanksgiving is about catching up with family members and eating turkey, but it may also be about seeing if a relocation is feasible for your particular financial situation,” Walker adds.

#18960. We keep coaching real estate agents to be salespeople. That was never the job

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (956 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

We keep coaching real estate agents to be salespeople. That was never the job

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (956 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, OPINION: Lance Pendleton argues that real estate agents are consultants, not salespeople.
  • According to recent reports, I was the national head of agent development at Compass, and I’ve been in front of more than 30,000 agents since.
  • The reason is simpler than anybody wants it to be.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, OPINION: Lance Pendleton argues that real estate agents are consultants, not salespeople. Learn what to ask before you pay for a coaching program.

According to recent reports, I was the national head of agent development at Compass, and I’ve been in front of more than 30,000 agents since. I’ve also sold the thing I’m about to take apart, so keep that in mind while you read.

You didn’t fail the program. The program failed you. How come?

The reason is simpler than anybody wants it to be. Nearly every coaching program in this business teaches professional sales skills to people who are not in sales. We’re consultants, advocates, advisors and educators.

Nobody has ever talked a family into a house they didn’t want to live in. What we do is help people through the largest and most emotional decision of their lives with the least amount of damage. We read a room. We tell someone the truth about their kitchen, and we hold a deal together at 9 p.m. on a Sunday when the buyer’s father has opinions.

That is not selling. We’re consultants, advocates, advisors and educators. If you can fog a mirror, you can get a license. Very few people can do those four things well, and I’ve yet to see a program that teaches them as a skill set.

This isn’t the coach’s fault. Coaches were trained the same way the rest of us were. Build the database. Reach as many people as you possibly can. Add value, and then add more of it tomorrow.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a word buried in there that I think is the dumbest one in our industry, and I say that with love. Value.

We all have the same value. Every one of us can pull a comp, open a door, write an offer and get to a closing table. What almost none of us have is a point of differentiation, the thing that tells a consumer specifically what you do for them and why it ought to be you. You can follow “add value” for a decade and stay interchangeable with the other four agents the seller interviewed.

There’s a second reason the homework never gets done: Agents live in two periods of time: now and not now.

Recent findings suggest that now is the pipe that burst three hours before a closing. Now is the appraisal, the inspection, the client calling at 10:30 p.m. about something that could have been a text. Now is loud, it’s permanent, and it pays this month. Not now is quiet and pays in three years, if at all.

The trouble is that everything producing long-term income security in this business sits in the not-now column. The National Association of Realtors’ 2026 member profile puts median gross income at $88,500 for agents with 16 years or more in the industry, and $8,000 for agents with two years or less.

The veterans report a median 49 percent of their business from repeat clients and another 32 percent from referrals. For the newest agents, both of those medians are zero.

Somebody will say that’s just arithmetic, that you need a past client before you can have a repeat one. That’s the point. The whole gap is 15 years of relationships, and not one hour of that work feels urgent on a Tuesday. This is a patient business being coached like an impatient one.

Sources indicate that we do something else I think is worse. We coach in a permanent state of enthusiasm. Everything is fabulous; every market is an opportunity; you’re crushing it; this is your year. I call that toxic positivity, and it does real damage. You sit in a hard month with two deals coming apart, you hear all of it, and you quietly conclude the problem must be you.

According to recent reports, what would help is unglamorous. This job burns through five things: prioritization, organization, time management, impulse control and emotional regulation. By Thursday of an ordinary week, most good agents are running low on at least two.

There’s nothing wrong with any of those people. Real support builds bumpers around those five, the same reason a bowling lane for kids has them. You don’t make the gutter disappear by concentrating harder.

That work means dealing with people as they are, for who they are. Not more, more, more. Not the next great thing. One thing, chosen for that person, small enough to start on a Thursday when everything else has gone sideways.

According to recent reports, we haven’t served this business well on that, and I include myself. I’ve sold the four-week cycle. It’s a comfortable thing to sell, because Week 1 always works.

If you’re picking a program this fall, ask what gets cut. Anybody can hand you 15 things. The one worth paying is the person who tells you which one matters and which 14 you can skip.

It has been revealed that we’re not in sales. We never were. Until the coaching in this business is built for that job, we’ll keep running very good people through programs that leave them feeling like the problem.

It has been revealed that you aren’t the problem. This is still the best time there’s ever been to be a great agent. We just have to stop training you for somebody else’s job.

The views and opinions expressed here are those of the contributor and separate from the Inman newsroom.

It has been revealed that lance Pendleton is the founder of Reframe Lab, a coaching and consulting practice for real estate agents, and the former national head of agent development at Compass in Connecticut. Get connected on Instagram.

Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, spent $228.1 million buying back its STRC preferred stock between Nov. 9 and Nov. 15, according to the tech giant's newly introduced filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Over the same period, Strategy bought 485 BTC for $33.4 million, so the company spent almost seven times more on STRC than on Bitcoin.

It has been revealed that "Strategy has acquired 485 BTC and repurchased $228M of STRC. As of 11/15/26, we hold 850,849 BTC and $4.9B of USD Assets," Michael Saylor wrote on X.

Sources indicate that the filing shows that Strategy sold 2.09 million shares of its Class A common stock and raised $244.7 million. The organization used $206.3 million of that amount for STRC buybacks and added another $21.8 million from interest earned on its dollar reserves.

The 485 BTC were bought at an average price of $68,887 per coin. The remaining $5 million from the share sales stayed on the books as free cash.

STRC, also known as Stretch, is a perpetual preferred stock with a variable monthly dividend, and Strategy rolled out it in July 2025.

When the price of Bitcoin slipped below $65,000, STRC fell to $99.08. Strategy aims to keep STRC close to its $100 par value, and the company has another $332.2 million set aside for buybacks. The board of Strategy also approved a December STRC dividend at an annual rate of 12%, or $1.00 per share.

"USD Duration is 3.4 yrs and STRC's BTC Credit tightened to 67 bps (-3 bps), assuming 10% BTC ARR, 40% BTC Vol, and a BTC price of $68,800," Saylor added.

As of Nov. 15, Strategy held 850,849 BTC, bought for a total of $64.2 billion at an average price of $75,452 per coin. On Monday, the price of Bitcoin stands at $63,941, and Strategy's holdings are worth around $54.4 billion.

Sources indicate that the unrealized loss of the firm on its Bitcoin holdings stands at around $9.8 billion. On Sunday, when the price of Bitcoin fell to $62,029 on Bitfinex, the loss was above $11 billion.

Strategy also holds $4.9 billion in dollar assets, and $4.75 billion of that amount is in its dedicated USD reserve.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, bitcoin critic Peter Schiff has once again predicted that Strategy will be forced to sell its Bitcoin stash to defend the unrealistic yields of its controversial STRC stock. Schiff, known for his crypto-skeptic tweets, has again mentioned STRC is under pressure after total BTC holdings plummeted more than $10 billion in value following the latest market squeeze.

Sources indicate that schiff highlighted that even with the latest buyback programs, STRC is likely to face further pressure and, eventually, Strategy will be forced to burn through its cash reserves, including USDT and then Bitcoin itself. The only alternative, he suggests, is to raise or suspend the dividend, which will tank the stock price and send the whole Saylor initiative further down the abyss.

Industry observers note that STRC is a variable-yield perpetual preferred stock issued by Strategy, which is the largest corporate Bitcoin holder. The stock was used to raise funds to fuel Saylor’s aggressive BTC buying strategy. The shares are designed to trade near $100, with monthly adjustments based on their dividend rate, which is at the moment as high as 12% and paid daily.

It has been revealed that while Bitcoin proponents initially welcomed Saylor’s flamboyant approach, they have generally become skeptical of the complex offering because of its risk and complexity. CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju, among others, has criticized it over the years. He believes that Saylor has made a habit of buying the digital currency at relative highs, putting STRC under further pressure. It has become a running joke that whenever Saylor buys, it marks a relative top and a sign for short-term traders to sell.

Here is the graph of all Strategy BTC buys:.

Recent Strategy buys confirm this unfortunate Saylor trend of buying BTC at its relative highs. It is not Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA) by any stretch of imagination, as STRC comes under pressure with each dip, and Saylor simply doesn’t have enough funds to purchase the crypto at that time.

So, Schiff is by no means an isolated critic of the STRC stock. The move has invited criticism from the industry’s own players. However, Schiff is connecting STRC directly to BTC, even though it is a corporate decision and has no relation to the decentralized cryptocurrency’s ecosystem. He has predicted the fall of the top cryptocurrency by market capitalization for most of the last 13 years. However, this time he could be proven right, as BTC remains in relative free fall, and with each dip, STRC drops into deeper trouble.

Tech Roundup: Zillow Preview listings go live in RealScout
